svg.text: The certificate to Mosquitto: copy, permit, reload
Concept 8 · Caddy asks for the mqtt.yourname.my.id certificate, Mosquitto uses its COPY on door 8883
then Exited (0); only now may Mosquitto start
without the copier, Mosquitto reads Caddy's cupboard directly → Permission denied, the broker stops
Let's Encrypt's issuer folder: acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory (simulated lab: pebble-14000-dir)
the order: web asks for the certificate, mqtt-certificate waits for its file (≤ 5 minutes), then copies, only then mosquitto starts
After a new copy: reload the VPS broker (on the Pi gateway: restart, not HUP)
simulated lab; "a key with the wrong owner" = a copy made by hand as root
log Reloading config.; the same PID, RestartCount 0
a key with the wrong owner: Error when reloading certificate
→ the broker keeps running with the old certificate
a key with the wrong owner: crash loop,

text.tspan: Unable to load server key file

svg.text: the bridge and the devices drop
Docker records it as stopped: the broker
isn't started again after a crash or a
reboot; the right way: the signal from
Renewal: Caddy renews by itself, Mosquitto does NOT re-read by itself
small lines = the cron every Monday 03:17 (VPS time)
One cron line on the VPS (crontab -e), without a line break
the script: docker compose run --rm mqtt-certificate,
then docker compose exec -T mosquitto kill -HUP 1
Simulated lab (Pebble, a 600 s lifetime): 443 already has the new
serial, 8883 keeps the old one until the script; then the new one,
the same PID, no new New bridge connected.
Forgotten until expiry: a bridge already connected
keeps running; a NEW connection is refused certificate has expired.
docker compose up -d copies too but does NOT reload:
that's why the HUP still runs every week.
